# 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 382r–382v

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** When David was old and full of days, he made Solomon his son king over Israel.

**2** He gathered together all the leaders of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.

**3** The Levites, thirty years old and upward, were numbered, and the total was thirty-eight thousand men.

**4** "Of these," David said, "twenty-four thousand shall have charge of the work in the house of the LORD, six thousand shall be officers and judges,

**5** four thousand shall be gatekeepers, and four thousand shall offer praises to the LORD with the instruments that I have made for praise."

**6** David organized them in divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

**7** Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.

**8** The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel — three.

**9** The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran — three. These were the heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan.

**10** The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei — four.

**11** Jahath was the chief and Zizah the second. But Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as a single father's house.

**12** The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel — four.

**13** The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things — he and his sons forever — to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to him, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever.

**14** As for Moses the man of God, his sons were counted among the tribe of Levi.

**15** The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

**16** The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.

**17** The sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.

**18** The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.

**19** The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.

**20** The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.

**21** The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.

**22** Eleazar died having no sons, only daughters; their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them.

**23** The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth — three.

**24** These were the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses — the heads of fathers' houses as they were registered according to the number of names of individuals from twenty years old and upward — who were to do the work for the service of the house of the LORD.

**25** For David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.

**26** And so the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service."

**27** For by the last words of David, the Levites were numbered from twenty years old and upward.

**28** Their duty was to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD, having charge of the courts, the chambers, the purification of all holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God;

**29** to care for the rows of bread, the flour for the grain offering, the unleavened wafers, the baked offerings, the offerings mixed with oil, and all measures of quantity and size;

**30** and to stand every morning, thanking and praising the LORD, and likewise at evening,

**31** and whenever burnt offerings were offered to the LORD on Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed feasts, according to the number required of them, as a regular duty before the LORD.

**32** Thus they were to keep charge of the tent of meeting and the sanctuary, and to attend to the sons of Aaron, their kindred, in the service of the house of the LORD.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter opens the great administrative section of 1 Chronicles (chs. 23-27), in which David organizes the temple personnel before his death. The Levites are divided by their three ancestral branches (Gershon, Kohath, Merari) and assigned four categories of service: temple work (24,000), administration and justice (6,000), gatekeeping (4,000), and music (4,000). The most theologically significant detail is the Aaron/Moses distinction (vv.13-14): Aaron's line receives permanent priestly consecration ("most holy things... forever"), while Moses' descendants are ordinary Levites. The chapter also contains an internal tension — the counting age shifts from thirty (v.3) to twenty (vv.24, 27), attributed to David's "last words." This revision reflects the practical shift from a portable tabernacle to a permanent temple: younger Levites can serve because the heavy carrying work is done. The Chronicler presents David not only as warrior and worshipper but as bureaucratic organizer — the man who designs the institutional framework that will sustain Israel's worship for centuries.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "full of days" vs. "had lived a full life"
- **EMET:** "full [save'a] of-days"
- **LOGOS:** "full of days"
- **PNEUMA:** "had lived a full life"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "full of days" — a biblical idiom (Gen 25:8; Job 42:17) that should be preserved rather than paraphrased.

### V.4-5 — "officers" vs. "administrators"
- **EMET:** "officers [shoterim] and-judges [shoftim]"
- **LOGOS:** "officers and judges"
- **PNEUMA:** "administrators and judges"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "officers and judges" — *shoterim* in its biblical usage denotes officials who enforce and organize, closer to "officers" than the modern-sounding "administrators."

### V.13 — "to consecrate the most holy things" vs. "set apart for the most sacred duties"
- **EMET:** "to-consecrate-him as-most-holy [qodesh qodashim]"
- **LOGOS:** "to consecrate the most holy things"
- **PNEUMA:** "permanently set apart for the most sacred duties"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to consecrate the most holy things" — the Hebrew *lehaqdiysho qodesh qodashim* is ambiguous: the suffix *-o* could refer to Aaron himself or to the holy things. LOGOS takes the most holy things as the object of Aaron's consecrating work. EMET reads Aaron himself as consecrated *as* most holy. Both are grammatically possible. SOPHIA follows LOGOS, as the priestly function of consecrating sacred objects aligns with the three duties that follow (incense, ministry, blessing).

### V.14 — "named among" vs. "counted among" vs. "simply counted among"
- **EMET:** "were-called upon the-tribe of-Levi"
- **LOGOS:** "were named among the tribe of Levi"
- **PNEUMA:** "were simply counted among the tribe of Levi"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "were counted among the tribe of Levi" — PNEUMA's "simply" is an editorial addition that emphasizes the contrast with Aaron, which is real but should not be imposed on the text. LOGOS's "named among" is accurate but less clear than "counted among."

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
